channel.description: Recent content in Sync on Best of AI

item.title: Amplenote
item.description:
Amplenote treats notes and tasks as part of the same system. You write notes with a Markdown-like editor, link them together, and embed tasks that appear both in the note and in a central task list and calendar. Daily jots capture quick thoughts, and the calendar shows tasks and events alongside notes, so planning the day and recording information happen in one place.

Its task score is an unusual feature: each task gets a number based on its importance, urgency, and effort, and the app highlights the highest-scoring tasks so you know where to begin. A plugin system lets users extend the app with scripts, including features that connect to outside tools. The built-in AI assistant can summarize notes, brainstorm, rewrite text, and use the contents of your notes as context, and it works on web, mobile, and desktop.

item.title: Craft Docs
item.description: Craft aims to make notes and documents that look good. It works as a block-based editor where text, images, tables, and cards live in nested pages that you can reorganize easily. Native apps for Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch are fast and polished, with offline support, and there is also a web and Windows version. Daily notes and tasks cover personal organization, and Spaces and collections keep larger projects tidy.

item.title: Heptabase
item.description: Heptabase treats notes as cards that you place on whiteboards, group, and connect. Instead of a long document or a folder tree, you build up an understanding of a topic visually: a card for each idea, laid out next to related ones, with arrows and sections that show structure. It suits people who learn and plan by seeing the relationships among ideas, such as researchers, students, writers, and product thinkers.

item.title: Notion
item.description:
Notion lets people build their own workspace from simple pieces. A page can hold text, headings, checklists, images, embedded files, and databases, and databases can be shown as tables, boards, calendars, or galleries. Teams use it for wikis, meeting notes, project tracking, product roadmaps, and personal organization, and templates help people get started. Real-time collaboration, comments, and permissions make it work for teams as well as individuals.

The product has grown beyond notes. Notion Calendar and Notion Mail connect scheduling and email to the workspace, and Sites turns pages into public web pages. Notion AI adds writing help, summaries, translation, and question answering across your workspace and connected tools like Slack and Google Drive, plus agents that perform tasks. AI meeting notes capture and summarize calls. See the Notion AI entry for details on those features.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: Obsidian treats notes as local files. Everything you write is a Markdown document in a folder on your computer, so you own the data and can open it with any other editor. You connect notes with links, and the app shows backlinks and a graph view of how ideas relate. People use it for personal knowledge management, research, writing, journaling, and project notes, and many build large networks of thousands of linked notes over years.

item.title: RemNote
item.description: RemNote is built for students who want to learn what they write. In a typical note app, notes sit in a folder and are rarely reviewed. In RemNote, you mark terms and definitions inside your notes, and the app turns them into flashcards automatically, then schedules reviews with a spaced repetition algorithm so facts move into long-term memory. Notes are organized in an outline, and each line can link to others, which helps build a connected knowledge base.

item.title: Roam Research
item.description:
Roam helped popularize networked note-taking. Notes are organized as outlines of bullet blocks, and you link to other pages by typing double brackets. Every link creates a backlink on the page it points to, so you can see everywhere a concept is mentioned. Daily notes serve as a default home for new thoughts, and over time, links build a web of connected ideas without a rigid folder structure.

Its power comes from working at the block level. Any bullet can be referenced or embedded elsewhere, queries pull together blocks that match conditions, and attributes add structured data to notes. A graph view and a plugin ecosystem add visualization and automation, and keyboard-driven editing makes it fast for those who master it. Researchers, writers, and knowledge workers have used it for long-term thinking.

item.title: Tana
item.description:
Tana combines outlining with databases. Everything is a node in an outline, and tagging a node with a Supertag gives it fields and behavior, so a note about a person, a book, or a project becomes structured and can be queried and viewed in many ways. Backlinks connect related ideas.

AI is integrated into the workflow. It can transcribe meetings and turn them into tagged notes, fill in fields, and answer questions across a workspace, and it can act on commands users define. Voice capture makes it easy to record ideas on the go.
